1.summary: The elder writes to the chosen lady and her children whom he loves in truth, rejoices that some walk in the truth, urges them to love one another by obeying God's commands, warns against deceivers who deny Christ came in the flesh, and hopes to visit and talk face to face.
1.lookfor: Notice how truth and love are woven together, and the practical warning about hospitality.

insights.title: The chosen lady
insights.body: The letter is to the chosen lady and her children (1:1), and ends with greetings from the children of your chosen sister (1:13). Most read this as a church and its members, a sister church sending greetings.

insights.title: Truth
insights.body: Truth appears five times in the first four verses. For John, truth isn't only correct ideas but reality revealed in Jesus, who called himself the truth.

insights.title: Love one another
insights.body: Not a new commandment, but the one we had from the beginning: that we love one another (1:5). John repeats Jesus' words from the Last Supper.

insights.title: Love is obedience
insights.body: This is love, that we walk according to his commandments (1:6). Love isn't just feeling; it walks a path.

insights.title: Don't welcome them
insights.body: If anyone comes without this teaching, don't receive him into your house or greet him (1:10). Travelling teachers relied on hosts; to host them was to sponsor their message. The warning is about supporting false teaching, not about refusing ordinary kindness.

insights.title: Go too far
insights.body: Whoever goes ahead and doesn't remain in the teaching of Christ doesn't have God (1:9). The false teachers claimed to be advanced; John says they had left the road.

insights.title: Paper and ink
insights.body: I'd rather not write with paper and ink; I hope to come and speak face to face, so our joy may be full (1:12). Some things are better said in person.

insights.title: Truth and love together
insights.body: John holds truth and love together. Do you tend to lean more toward one than the other?

intro.who: The elder (1:1), traditionally the apostle John, the same writer as 1 John. Elder may mean an older, respected leader.
intro.when: About AD 85–100, probably from Ephesus, around the time of 1 John.
intro.why: A short note to the chosen lady and her children, most likely a local church and its members. It urges them to keep loving one another and walking in the truth, and not to welcome travelling teachers who deny that Jesus Christ came in the flesh.

outline.title: Truth and love; don't host deceivers
